ios.head: All the funnel steps are moving together (up about +57.4%) — nothing out of step.
ios.body: New User, Install and New Subs are all moving by roughly the same amount (about +57.4%, none more than 5 percentage points away). Nothing is out of step for this selection.

android.head: US is doing worse than YMK overall on App Total Revenue (-20.9% vs -11.2%).
android.body: App Total Revenue for US is -20.9%, while YMK overall is -11.2% — a gap of -9.6pp. US is holding the overall number down.

android.head: Expect App Total Revenue to weaken in about 7 days — fewer of the people installing are subscribing.
android.body: App Total New Subs is -59.8% while App Total Install is -44.0% — fewer of the people who installed are subscribing (-15.8pp less growth). New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So expect App Total Revenue to weaken in about 7 days.

android.head: App Total Revenue -20.9% does not match new subs +5.4% from 7 days earlier — this drop is not coming from new customers.
android.body: App Total Revenue on 10-31 vs 10-24 is -20.9%, but App Total New Subs on 10-24 vs 10-17 was +5.4% — they did not move together. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the subscription revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. By purchase type (on 10-31 vs 10-24): Subscription -20.0%, Pay as you go -37.6%. Since new subs moved the other way while Subscription revenue (-20.0%) did not follow them, this drop is coming from existing customers instead: check renewals and cancellations, refunds, or a recent price change — not marketing or installs.

android.head: Subscription revenue is down 21.9%; Pay as you go +15.2% is softening it (total -20.9%).
android.body: App Total Revenue (YMK · US) was 2,298, against 2,904 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks (-606). By purchase type: Subscription -618 (-21.9%), Pay as you go +12 (+15.2%). Pay as you go is 4.0% of revenue. The recurring part is what new subs feed, so the Pay as you go lift is one-off cover, not a recovery.

android.body: Paid Install (YMK · US) was 771, +5.3% against the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks, while total installs moved -44.0% — a difference of +49.3 percentage points. Paid Install is now 100.0% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving toward it.

ios.head: App Total Install +126.5% — Organic Install is behind most of it (+4,050, +360.7%).
ios.body: App Total Install (YMK · US) was 8,905, against 3,932 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks — a change of +4,973. Where that came from: Organic Install +4,050 (+360.7%), Paid Install +952 (+36.5%), SEO Install +10 (+11.7%). Organic Install moved the most on its own (+4,050, +360.7%) and is now 58.1% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first.

insights.title: Install mix — Where installs come from is shifting away from SEO Install (-11.9% vs +2.1% for installs overall).
insights.body: SEO Install was 1,853, -11.9% against the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks, while total installs moved +2.1% — a difference of -14.0 percentage points. SEO Install is now 5.9% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving away from it; free traffic slipping while paid holds up means we are buying more of the same installs..

insights.title: Which app — App Total New User -8.7% is mostly YCP — not every app.
insights.body: App Total New User moved -8.7% overall, but the apps are far apart (All App -8.7%, YMK +28.3%, YCP -91.2%, YCV +8.0%, YCE -2.7%, YCA +0.6%). YCP accounts for most of it, so look at what changed in that one app rather than something affecting all of them.
